type: pilot/mid-work -- STOPPING HERE, board-wide finding, awaiting operator direction
headline: parcel-record-fill.mjs unconditionally clobbers every 'companion'-grain rail (17+ rails including flood, wells, specialDistricts, valueHistory, permits, easements, ossf, owner, salesHistory, and more) back to the engine's default 'unaccounted' state EVERY TIME IT RUNS FOR A COUNTY, regardless of whether a separate specialized job already populated that rail correctly. This is code-verified, not inferred from timing alone, and it is happening on a recurring, ongoing basis -- including a parcel-record-fill execution for Williamson (48491) that is RUNNING RIGHT NOW (started 2026-09-02T16:23:02.769Z, still status=running as of this checkpoint).

mechanismConfirmedByReadingCode.trace: instantiateAndIngest() calls instantiateParcelRecord() for every propId in the county, which (per src/lib/parcel-record-engine/rail-keys.js) generates a default cell for ALL declared rails including every 'companion'-grain rail -- flood among them (rail-keys.js line 66). ingestCadOntoRecords() and ingestJurisdictionOntoRecords() then overlay CAD/jurisdiction-derived values onto the rails parcel-record-fill itself owns -- flood is not among them; it is owned exclusively by the separate flood-ingest.mjs job. upsertRecords() then calls flattenCellStates(rec) for EVERY rail on EVERY record (no filter for 'rails this job owns') and batch-upserts all of them via UPSERT_CELLS_BATCH_SQL, whose ON CONFLICT (place_key, rail_key) DO UPDATE SET cell_state = EXCLUDED.cell_state unconditionally overwrites whatever was already stored -- including a real 'value' or 'absent-verified' state written by a different job -- with the freshly-generated default 'unaccounted' cell.
mechanismConfirmedByReadingCode.secondMechanismConsideredAndRejected: Initially considered the just-merged PARCEL-S6-COLLISION remediation (PR #73, which also touches parcel-record-fill.mjs) as the cause, since its own dispatch explicitly warns 'idempotent upserts SKIP, they do not CLEAR' and describes a targeted reset -- but scoped to 134 groups / 777 accounts' dollar cells only, three orders of magnitude smaller than the ~900,000 flood cells observed reset. Rejected once the runs table showed parcel-record-fill executions (phase='parcel-record-fill', not 'flood-ingest' or an S6-specific phase) at 12:45:11-14Z and 12:59:54-55Z across ALL SIX counties simultaneously, and the Williamson flood-ingest run's timeline (10:38:20Z-15:00:15Z) showed a clean split at exactly those two clobber instants: 71,963 'value' rows survive (written after the LAST clobber at 12:59:55) and 210,600 do not (written before it and never re-run since). Code-reading (the upsert SQL itself) confirmed the mechanism directly rather than resting on the timing correlation alone.
